questions.question: Identify the incorrect sentence.

options.text: All of the cities in California is being affected by the rain yesterday.
Seven people were rescued from the fire.
Half of the boxes are empty.
Some of the TV programs are very interesting.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Option 1: "All of the cities in California is being affected by the rain yesterday" is incorrect because:
 
 
• The sentence uses incorrect tense and subject-verb agreement.
 
• "Is being affected" is grammatically incorrect for past events. Instead, "were affected" should be used to indicate a completed action in the past.
 
• The correct form of the sentence would be: "All of the cities in California were affected by the rain yesterday."
 
 
 
• Option 2: "Seven people were rescued from the fire" is correct. The sentence uses proper past tense and is grammatically accurate.
 
• Option 3: "Half of the boxes are empty" is correct. It uses proper plural subject-verb agreement and is grammatically accurate.
 
• Option 4: "Some of the TV programs are very interesting" is correct. It uses proper plural subject-verb agreement and is grammatically accurate.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:** 
 
 
• The verb must agree with the subject in both number and tense.
 
• For example: 
 
 
• Correct: "He runs every morning." (Singular subject matches singular verb)
 
• Correct: "They run every morning." (Plural subject matches plural verb)
 
 
 
 
 
• **Past Tense Usage:** 
 
 
• Past tense is used to describe actions that have already been completed.
 
• Example: "She walked to the park yesterday."
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is free from grammatical error?

options.text: She is senior than me by two years.
He was prevented to go out by the guard.
I look forward to meet you soon.
The manager, as well as his assistants, was late.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**To identify the sentence that is free from error, let's analyze the prepositional and structural rules in each option:**

__
 
• **Option 1: She is senior than me by two years.**

 
 
• Adjectives ending in "-ior" (such as senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior) are followed by the preposition "to," not "than."
 
• The sentence is erroneous__.
 
• **The correct sentence would be:** "She is senior **to** me by two years."
 
 
 
• **Option 2: He was prevented to go out by the guard.**
 __
 
• The verb "prevented" must be followed by the preposition "from" and a gerund (verb+ing), not an infinitive ("to go").
 
• The sentence is erroneous__.
 
• **The correct sentence would be:** "He was prevented **from going** out by the guard."
 
 
 
• **Option 3: I look forward to meet you soon.**
 __
 
• In the phrase "look forward to," the word "to" is a preposition, not part of an infinitive. Therefore, it must be followed by a noun or a gerund.
 
• The sentence is erroneous__.
 
• **The correct sentence would be:** "I look forward to **meeting** you soon."
 
 
 
• **Option 4: The manager, as well as his assistants, was late.**
 __
 
• When a subject is connected by phrases like "as well as," "along with," or "together with," the verb agrees only with the **first subject**. Since "The manager" is singular, the singular verb "was" is correct.
 
• This sentence is grammatically and contextually correct__.
 
 
 
• __Therefore, out of the given options, only sentence 4 is free from grammatical error__.

questions.solution:

• In this sentence, despite the warning of heavy rain, the outdoor ceremony proceeded. This indicates a contrast, making **"Even though"** the appropriate choice.
 
• **Options 2, 3**, and **4** do not fit the context because they do not convey contrast:
 
 
• **Option 2 ("Because"):** Indicates cause-effect, which is incorrect here.

• **Option 4 ("Since"):** Indicates cause or time, which does not align with the sentence's context of contrast.

options.text: He said, "The machine operated automatically but had malfunctioned that morning."
He said, "The machine operated automatically but had malfunctioned this morning."
He said, "The machine operates automatically, but malfunctioned this morning." morning."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He said that the machine operates automatically but had malfunctioned that morning.
 
• **Key Conversions from Indirect to Direct:**
 
 
• **General Truth/Permanent State:**
 
 
• The verb **"operates"** remains in the simple present tense because it describes a general fact or a permanent characteristic of the machine. When a statement is a universal/permanent truth, the tense does not necessarily back-shift even if the reporting verb is in the past.
 
 
 
• **Tense Change (Past Perfect to Simple Past):**
 
 
• The past perfect **"had malfunctioned"** in indirect speech typically converts back to the simple past **"malfunctioned"** in direct speech to represent a completed action in the past.
 
 
 
• **Time Expression:**
 
 
• The phrase **"that morning"** is converted back to **"this morning"** in direct speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Structure:** The conjunction "that" is removed, and the speaker's exact words are enclosed in quotation marks, preceded by a comma.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He said, 'The machine operates automatically, but malfunctioned this morning.'"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Incorrect because it uses "operated" (changing a general fact to a past event) and fails to change "that morning" to "this morning."
 
• **Option 2:** Incorrect because it uses "operated," which would normally back-shift to "had operated" in indirect speech, unlike the original sentence.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect because it uses the present continuous "is operating," which would change to "was operating" in indirect speech.

questions.question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

The students were made to write a detailed summary of the complex text.

options.text: They made the students write a detailed summary of the complex text.
The students wrote a detailed summary of the complex text.
They made the students to write a detailed summary of the complex text.
The students were made that they should write a detailed summary.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tense Identification:** The original sentence "were made" is in the **Simple Past Passive** voice.
 
• **Active Voice Rule:** To convert Simple Past Passive to Active, the structure changes from "was/were made + to + V1" to "**made + [Object] + V1 (bare infinitive)**".
 
• **Special Rule for "Make":** In the passive voice, "make" is followed by a full infinitive (**to write**). However, in the active voice, "make" is a causative verb followed by a bare infinitive (**write** without "to").
 
• **Subject Placement:** Since the passive sentence does not specify who "made" the students do the work, a placeholder subject like "They" is introduced.
 
• **Maintaining Meaning:** Option 1 correctly applies the causative verb rule and maintains the original past tense context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"They made the students write a detailed summary of the complex text."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "The students wrote..." removes the causative element ("made"), changing the meaning from being forced to doing it voluntarily.
 
• **Option 3:** "made the students **to** write" is grammatically incorrect in the active voice; "make" requires the bare infinitive (no "to").
 
• **Option 4:** "The students were made that..." is an ungrammatical and awkward construction that does not follow standard English syntax.

__

• **Key Conversions:**

• The first-person pronoun **"I"** changes to the third-person **"she"** because it refers to the speaker.

questions.question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

Did the renowned author finally release the highly anticipated sequel to his award-winning novel?

options.text: Was the highly anticipated sequel to his award-winning novel finally released by the renowned author?
Has the highly anticipated sequel to his award-winning novel been finally released by the renowned author?
Was the highly anticipated sequel to his award-winning novel been released by the renowned author?
Did the highly anticipated sequel to his award-winning novel be released by the renowned author?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tense Identification:** The original sentence "Did... release" is an interrogative (question) form of the **Simple Past** tense.
 
• **Passive Voice Rule:** To convert a Simple Past question into Passive Voice, the structure is: **Was/Were + Subject + V3 (Past Participle)?**
 
• **Subject-Object Swap:** The object of the active sentence ("the highly anticipated sequel...") becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• **Verb Conversion:** The auxiliary "Did" is replaced by "Was" (because "sequel" is singular), and the base verb "release" changes to its V3 form, "released."
 
• **Adverb Placement:** The adverb "finally" is placed before the main verb "released" to maintain the flow and meaning of the original sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Was the highly anticipated sequel to his award-winning novel finally released by the renowned author?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "Has... been finally released" changes the tense to Present Perfect, which is not the tense of the original sentence.
 
• **Option 3:** "Was... been released" is grammatically incorrect because "was" and "been" cannot be used together in this manner for the Simple Past.
 
• **Option 4:** "Did... be released" is an incorrect construction; "did" is not used as an auxiliary in standard passive voice transformations.

questions.question: A and B start a business with ₹2000 and ₹3000 respectively. After 1 year, total profit is ₹1000. Find B's share.

B's investment = ₹3000

Profit share ratio = Investment of A : Investment of B

B's share = (B's ratio ÷ Total ratio) × Total profit

⇒ Profit share ratio = 2 : 3

⇒ Total ratio = 2 + 3 = 5

⇒ B's share = (3 ÷ 5) × 1000

questions.question: A train 120 meters long passes a man running at 6 km/h in the same direction in 6 seconds. What is the speed of the train?

Time = 6 s

Relative speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Relative speed = 120 ÷ 6 = 20 m/s

⇒ Speed of man = 6 × 5 ÷ 18 = 5/3 m/s

⇒ Speed of train = (60 + 5) ÷ 3 = 65/3 m/s

⇒ Speed of train = 65/3 × 18 ÷ 5

⇒ Speed of train = 78 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 78.**

questions.question: At which of the following places was the inscription of Pratihara king Nagabhata found?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **inscription of Pratihara king Nagabhata** was discovered in **Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh**. This inscription is of historical importance as it provides insights into the achievements and reign of the Pratihara dynasty.
 
• The inscription highlights the military conquests of **Nagabhata I**, who was a key ruler of the Pratihara dynasty. He is credited with successfully defending his territories against Arab invasions.
 
• The Pratiharas, also known as Gurjara-Pratiharas, played a crucial role in the early medieval period of Indian history, particularly in northern India. They were known for their contributions to art, architecture, and culture.
 
• The Gwalior inscription is written in **Sanskrit** and provides valuable information about the socio-political and economic conditions of the time, as well as the administrative capabilities of the Pratihara rulers.
 
• **Gwalior**, located in present-day Madhya Pradesh, served as a significant political and cultural center during the reign of the Pratiharas and is renowned for its historic monuments and inscriptions.

• **Pratihara Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Pratihara dynasty was a prominent ruling dynasty in northern India during the 8th–11th centuries. They are also known as the Gurjara-Pratiharas.
 
• Their empire extended from Gujarat to Bengal at its peak, and they were known for their military strength in resisting Arab invasions.
 
• They contributed significantly to temple architecture, particularly in regions like Khajuraho and Kannauj.
 
 
 
• **Gwalior:**
 
 
• Gwalior is a historic city in Madhya Pradesh, known for its rich cultural heritage and architectural marvels like the Gwalior Fort and ancient temples.
 
• The Gwalior inscription of Nagabhata I is one of the many historical records found in this city, shedding light on India's medieval history.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh:** Known for its Buddhist stupas and sculptures, Amaravati was not associated with the Pratihara dynasty.
 
• **Agra, Uttar Pradesh:** While historically significant, Agra is not linked to inscriptions of the Pratihara dynasty.
 
• **Kandahar, Afghanistan:** Kandahar has historical significance due to its role in ancient and medieval trade routes but is unrelated to the Pratihara inscriptions.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Inscriptions:**
 
 
• Inscriptions serve as primary sources of historical information, providing details about rulers, their achievements, and the socio-economic conditions of their times.
 
• The Gwalior inscription of Nagabhata I is a testament to the administrative and military prowess of the Pratihara dynasty.

The correct answer is __**Shanghai Cooperation Organisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS)** is a permanent organ of the **Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)**, which is focused on addressing terrorism, separatism, and extremism in the region.
 
• The headquarters of RATS is located in **Tashkent, Uzbekistan**, and it plays a pivotal role in fostering regional cooperation on security matters.
 
• RATS promotes intelligence sharing, joint counter-terrorism exercises, and the coordination of operations between member states to combat transnational threats.
 
• SCO, established in **2001**, is an intergovernmental organization that primarily aims to enhance political, economic, and security cooperation among its members, which include countries like **China, Russia, India, Pakistan**, and others.
 
• Through RATS, SCO member states work together to counter issues such as terrorist financing, cyberterrorism, and the proliferation of extremist ideologies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO):**

 
 
• The SCO is a political, economic, and security alliance originally founded by **China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan** in **2001**. It later expanded to include **India** and **Pakistan** in **2017**.
 
• SCO's goals include promoting peace, stability, and development in the region, as well as combating terrorism, drug trafficking, and organized crime.
 
• It is considered one of the world's largest regional organizations, covering a significant portion of the Eurasian continent.
 
 
 
• **RATS Structure and Functions:**
 
 
• RATS acts as a coordination center for member states to combat terrorism, separatism, and extremism.
 
• It facilitates regular meetings, the exchange of intelligence, and the development of joint strategies to counter regional security challenges.
 
• RATS also focuses on issues related to cybersecurity, such as addressing cyberterrorism and ensuring safe digital communication.
 
 
 
• **Key SCO Initiatives:**
 
 
• Joint military exercises such as the **“Peace Mission”** drills, aimed at strengthening counter-terrorism capabilities.
 
• Promotion of regional economic connectivity through initiatives like the **Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)** and regional trade agreements.
 
• Cultural and educational exchanges to foster mutual understanding and cooperation among member states.
 
 
 
• **Important Points about Other Options:**
 
 
• **BRICS:** A group of five major emerging economies – Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa – focused on economic cooperation and development but not directly associated with RATS.
 
• **Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC):** Comprises 57 member states and is focused on promoting solidarity among Islamic countries; it does not have a specific anti-terror body like RATS.
 
• **SAARC:** The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation aims to promote development and cooperation in South Asia but has no direct affiliation with RATS.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **SCO Member States:** The organization consists of eight permanent members: China, Russia, India, Pakistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan. Observer states include Iran, Afghanistan, Belarus, and Mongolia.
 
• **RATS Achievements:** RATS has contributed to enhancing regional security through intelligence sharing, capacity building, and joint counter-terrorism operations.
 
• **Significance of SCO:** With its focus on security and economic integration, SCO plays a critical role in stabilizing Central Asia and fostering cooperation between Eurasian nations.
 
• **Challenges:** Despite its achievements, SCO faces challenges such as differing political ideologies among members and the complex geopolitical environment of the region.

questions.question: In March 2025, which High court division bench comprising Justice C S Sudha questioned the extent to which the state can interfere in regulating violence in visual media?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala High Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kerala High Court:** In **March 2025**, a division bench of the **Kerala High Court** comprising Justice C S Sudha raised concerns about the **extent of state interference** in regulating violence depicted in visual media. This query emerged due to debates about balancing artistic freedom and societal impact.
 
• **Freedom of Expression:** The court highlighted the significance of **Article 19(1)(a) of the Indian Constitution**, which guarantees the **freedom of speech and expression**, while also questioning whether this freedom can be curtailed to limit violent imagery in visual media.
 
• **Social Responsibility:** The bench emphasized the potential **impact of violence in visual media** on societal behavior, particularly its influence on young and impressionable minds, sparking debates on ethical filmmaking and censorship.
 
• **Regulatory Framework:** The court explored the role of existing regulatory mechanisms like the **Cinematograph Act, 1952**, and the **Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC)** in maintaining a balance between creative freedom and societal interests.
 
• **Kerala's Cultural Perspective:** Kerala, known for its vibrant film industry, often engages in debates around the **intersection of culture, media, and law**. The High Court's observations reflect this ongoing discourse on responsible filmmaking and media representation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 19(1)(a) of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• **Guarantees freedom of speech and expression** to citizens of India.
 
• While this freedom is fundamental, it is subject to **reasonable restrictions** under Article 19(2) for purposes such as **public order, decency, morality, and sovereignty of India**.
 
 
 
• **Cinematograph Act, 1952:**
 
 
• This Act governs the certification of films for public exhibition in India.
 
• The **Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC)** is the regulatory authority that determines the suitability of a film for public viewing based on various criteria, including depictions of violence.
 
• It plays a crucial role in implementing censorship guidelines.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Visual Media:**
 
 
• Visual media, including films and television, has a profound influence on societal behavior and norms.
 
• Studies indicate that prolonged exposure to violent content can **normalize aggression** and desensitize audiences to real-world violence.
 
• Debates around media regulation often center on the need to balance **creative freedom** with **social responsibility**.
 
 
 
• **Kerala's Film Industry:**
 
 
• Kerala is renowned for its **progressive and socially conscious cinema**, often addressing themes like caste, gender, and political issues.
 
• The state's filmmakers frequently navigate the intersection of **artistic expression** and societal impact, making it a hub for discussions on media ethics.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC):**

 
 
• The CBFC classifies films into categories like **U (Universal), UA (Parental Guidance), and A (Adult)**, based on their content.
 
• It aims to ensure that films adhere to **cultural and legal norms** while respecting creative liberties.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Oversight:**
 
 
• Indian courts often intervene in cases where **freedom of expression** and **public interest** clash, ensuring that both are upheld in balance.
 
• Judgments like the Kerala High Court's observations contribute to the evolving discourse on media regulation.
 
 
 
• **Relevance of Media Ethics:**
 
 
• Media ethics emphasize the **responsibility of creators** to produce content that is socially constructive.
 
• This includes adhering to **standards of decency, accuracy, and fairness**, particularly in visual media.

questions.question: As the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) completed 10 years in August 2024, which ministry oversees its implementation?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)** is a **flagship financial inclusion program** launched by the Government of India on **28th August 2014**.
 
• The scheme aims to provide **universal access to banking facilities**, including basic savings bank accounts, financial literacy, and access to credit, insurance, and pension services.
 
• The **Ministry of Finance** oversees its implementation, ensuring effective coordination across banks, financial institutions, and other stakeholders.
 
• The program is specifically designed to target the **unbanked population** in rural and urban areas, helping them integrate into the formal financial system.
 
• Under PMJDY, beneficiaries receive **zero-balance savings accounts**, a **RuPay debit card**, and accidental insurance cover of up to **Rs. 2 lakhs**. Additionally, an overdraft facility of up to **Rs. 10,000** is provided to eligible account holders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Features of PMJDY:**

 
 
• The scheme is aimed at providing **universal access to banking services** for every household in the country.
 
• It includes benefits such as **direct benefit transfers (DBT)**, social security schemes like **PM Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)** and **PM Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)**, and pension schemes like the **Atal Pension Yojana (APY)**.
 
• Accounts opened under PMJDY have grown substantially over the years, with over **50 crore beneficiaries** as of **2023**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Finance:**
 
 
• The Ministry of Finance is one of the key ministries in the Government of India, responsible for managing the country's **economic policy, government finances, and financial regulations**.
 
• It oversees various departments, including the **Department of Financial Services**, which plays a pivotal role in implementing schemes like PMJDY.
 
• The Ministry also ensures the success of financial inclusion initiatives by collaborating with public sector banks, private banks, and regional rural banks (RRBs).
 
 
 
• **Impact of PMJDY:**
 
 
• PMJDY has significantly contributed to **financial inclusion** by bringing millions of unbanked individuals into the formal banking system.
 
• It has facilitated the implementation of direct benefit transfers, reducing **leakages in subsidy disbursements** and promoting transparency.
 
• The scheme has also empowered women and rural populations by providing them with access to financial services, enabling **economic empowerment**.
 
 
 
• **Other Relevant Ministries:**
 
 
• **Ministry of Home Affairs:** Responsible for internal security and law enforcement.
 
• **Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare:** Oversees agricultural development and welfare schemes for farmers.
 
• **Ministry of Defence:** Manages the defense and security of the nation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The PMJDY scheme is considered the **world's largest financial inclusion program**, recognized globally for its scale and impact.
 
• It has played a crucial role in implementing the **JAM trinity** (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile), which is central to India's digital economy framework.
 
• The scheme has been instrumental in providing financial stability to economically weaker sections, especially during crises like the **COVID-19 pandemic**.

questions.question: In Dravida style of architecture, the front wall has an entrance gateway in its centre, which is known as a_________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gopuram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gopuram** is the term used for the entrance gateway in Dravida style of temple architecture. It is a prominent architectural feature commonly seen in South Indian temples.
 
• The **Gopuram** serves as the monumental tower at the entrance of temple complexes and is often adorned with intricate carvings and sculptures depicting gods, goddesses, and mythological tales.
 
• In the Dravida style, the **Gopuram** is a towering structure that acts as a landmark and symbolizes the spiritual gateway to the temple.
 
• Historically, **Gopurams** were constructed to reflect the architectural and cultural grandeur of the respective dynasties, particularly during the reigns of the Chola, Pandya, and Vijayanagara empires.
 
• The construction of **Gopurams** was aimed at attracting devotees and showcasing the artistic excellence of temple builders in ancient India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dravida Style of Architecture:**

 
 
• The **Dravida style** of temple architecture flourished in South India, particularly under the Chola, Pallava, Pandya, and Vijayanagara dynasties.
 
• This style is characterized by pyramid-shaped towers called **Vimana** over the sanctum and the presence of ornate gateways known as **Gopurams**.
 
• The temples often include features such as pillared halls (**Mandapas**), water tanks, and elaborate sculptures.
 
• Examples of Dravida architecture include the **Brihadeshwara Temple** in Tamil Nadu and the **Meenakshi Temple** in Madurai.
 
 
 
• **Gopuram Features:**
 
 
• **Height:** Gopurams are tall structures, often rising several hundred feet, making them visible from great distances.
 
• **Decoration:** They are adorned with intricate carvings, colorful stucco figures, and representations of deities, celestial beings, and mythical creatures.
 
• **Purpose:** The Gopuram serves both religious and functional purposes, acting as a spiritual gateway and a marker for temple complexes.
 
 
 
• **Other Architectural Features:**
 
 
• **Pada:** Refers to the base or pedestal of the temple and is not related to the entrance gateway.
 
• **Prastara:** Denotes the horizontal layers of the superstructure and is unrelated to the entrance gateway.
 
• **Griva:** Refers to the neck or transitional part of the temple tower and does not represent the entrance gateway.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Famous Gopurams:**
 
 
• The **Raja Gopuram** at the Meenakshi Temple in Madurai.
 
• The **Gopuram** of the Brihadeshwara Temple in Thanjavur.
 
• The **Gopurams** of the Virupaksha Temple in Hampi.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** The construction of Gopurams reached its zenith during the Vijayanagara Empire, showcasing the grandeur and artistic excellence of South Indian temple architecture.
 
• **Cultural Significance:** Gopurams are not merely architectural elements but also serve as symbols of devotion, spirituality, and the cultural heritage of South India.
 
• **Modern Relevance:** Many Gopurams are now recognized as UNESCO World Heritage Sites, attracting millions of tourists and devotees annually.

questions.question: What is a disadvantage of friction?

options.text: It prevents objects from wearing out
It causes wear and tear of materials

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It causes wear and tear of materials**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Friction** is a resistive force that occurs when two surfaces come into contact and move relative to each other. While it has some advantages, it also has significant disadvantages, especially in mechanical applications.
 
• One major disadvantage of friction is that it **causes wear and tear** of materials. This happens because the continuous rubbing of surfaces damages their structural integrity over time.
 
• Friction leads to a reduction in the **lifespan of machinery and components**, as the constant abrasion deteriorates the material quality.
 
• In industries, wear and tear caused by friction can result in **higher maintenance costs**. Frequent replacement or repair of components is required to ensure the machinery functions properly.
 
• Friction also generates **heat**, which can further accelerate the degradation of materials, leading to issues such as overheating and thermal damage.
 
• Hence, minimizing friction through lubrication or advanced materials is a key focus in mechanical engineering to reduce wear and tear.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Advantages of Friction:**

 
 
• Friction is essential for performing tasks such as walking, driving, and holding objects. Without friction, movement would be uncontrollable.
 
• It helps in the braking systems of vehicles, allowing them to stop effectively.
 
• Friction plays a critical role in processes such as cutting, grinding, and polishing in manufacturing.
 
 
 
• **Methods to Reduce Friction:**
 
 
• Lubrication: Using oils or greases reduces the direct contact between surfaces, minimizing wear and tear.
 
• Using advanced materials such as **ceramics** or **polymers** with lower coefficients of friction can decrease the impact of friction.
 
• Implementing ball bearings or roller bearings reduces friction in rotating systems.
 
 
 
• **Types of Friction:**
 
 
• **Static Friction:** The frictional force that prevents relative motion between surfaces in contact.
 
• **Kinetic Friction:** The resistive force occurring during relative motion between surfaces.
 
• **Rolling Friction:** The friction that occurs when an object rolls over a surface.
 
• **Fluid Friction:** The resistance encountered by objects moving through fluids (liquids or gases).
 
 
 
• **Applications of Friction:**
 
 
• Friction is used in mechanical systems such as clutches and brakes for controlling motion.
 
• It is also utilized in sports to enhance grip, such as in climbing shoes or car tires.
 
• In construction, friction is exploited for fastening components, such as nails and screws.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Heat Generation:** Friction converts kinetic energy into thermal energy, which can lead to overheating in machines and devices.
 
• **Energy Loss:** Friction results in the loss of energy, reducing the efficiency of systems such as engines and turbines.
 
• **Material Degradation:** The repeated action of friction causes scratches, cracks, and deformation of surfaces over time.
 
• **Scientific Study:** The coefficient of friction is studied to design systems with optimal performance, balancing frictional force requirements.

questions.question: The Parker Solar Probe, launched to study the Sun by moving in a solar orbit, is a mission of which space agency?

__
 
• The **Parker Solar Probe** is a space mission launched by **NASA**, the space agency of the **United States**.
 
• It was launched on **August 12, 2018**, from Cape Canaveral, Florida, aboard a Delta IV Heavy rocket.
 
• The mission's primary objective is to study the **Sun's outer atmosphere (corona)** and understand phenomena such as **solar winds** and **solar energy particles**.
 
• The Parker Solar Probe is designed to get closer to the Sun than any previous spacecraft, reaching within **3.83 million miles (6.16 million kilometers)** of the Sun's surface.
 
• It is equipped with a **heat shield** made of carbon-composite materials to withstand temperatures of up to **2,500 degrees Fahrenheit (1,377 degrees Celsius)**.

__
 
• **About NASA:**

 
 
• **NASA** stands for the **National Aeronautics and Space Administration**.
 
• It was established in **1958** and is headquartered in **Washington, D.C.**, United States.
 
• NASA is responsible for civilian space exploration, aeronautics research, and scientific discovery.
 
• Some of NASA's notable missions include the **Apollo moon landings**, the **Voyager probes**, and the **Mars Perseverance Rover**.
 
 
 
• **About the Parker Solar Probe:**
 
 
• It was named after **Eugene Parker**, an astrophysicist who first proposed the concept of **solar winds**.
 
• The spacecraft uses advanced instruments like the **FIELDS Experiment** to measure electric and magnetic fields and the **WISPR telescope** to image the solar corona.
 
• The Parker Solar Probe aims to solve mysteries about the Sun, such as why the corona is hotter than the solar surface.
 
• This mission is expected to last until **2025** and will provide groundbreaking data for solar physics research.
 
 
 
• **Other Space Agencies:**
 
 
• **JAXA:** The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, headquartered in Japan, focuses on space research and satellite development.
 
• **ISRO:** The Indian Space Research Organisation, headquartered in Bengaluru, India, is known for missions like **Chandrayaan** and **Mangalyaan**.
 
• **CNES:** The French National Centre for Space Studies, headquartered in Paris, France, specializes in satellite systems and space exploration.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Parker Solar Probe:**

 
 
• It is the first spacecraft to fly into the Sun's corona, gathering data that will help scientists understand **space weather** and its impact on Earth.
 
• The mission contributes to forecasting solar storms, which can disrupt satellite communications and power grids.
 
• It provides insights into the fundamental processes of star formation and energy transfer.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Solar Research:**
 
 
• Understanding solar winds is crucial for protecting astronauts and spacecraft from radiation.
 
• The findings will enhance our knowledge of **stellar dynamics**, which impacts planetary systems.

questions.question: Who was architect of Indian Planning?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis**, often referred to as the "architect of Indian Planning," was a renowned Indian statistician and economist.
 
• He played a pivotal role in the formulation of India's **Second Five-Year Plan** (1956–1961), which emphasized the importance of industrialization and the growth of the public sector.
 
• Mahalanobis introduced the **Mahalanobis Model**, which focused on the development of heavy industries as the backbone of India's economy.
 
• He was the founder of the **Indian Statistical Institute (ISI)** and contributed significantly to the statistical and economic planning of the country.
 
• His contributions to India's economic planning earned him recognition as a key advisor to the **Planning Commission of India**, established in 1950.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Mahalanobis Model:**

 
 
• This model emphasized the allocation of resources to industries producing capital goods, such as steel, machinery, and infrastructure, to accelerate economic growth.
 
• It prioritized heavy industries over consumer goods industries, believing that this approach would lead to long-term economic stability.
 
• The model was integral to the **Second Five-Year Plan (1956–1961)** and had a lasting influence on India's economic policies.
 
 
 
• **Indian Statistical Institute (ISI):**
 
 
• The ISI was founded by Mahalanobis in **1931** in Kolkata to promote research and training in statistics.
 
• It became a key institution for developing statistical methods and their applications in various fields, including economics, biology, and social sciences.
 
 
 
• **Other Contributions:**
 
 
• Mahalanobis introduced the **Mahalanobis Distance**, a statistical measure used widely in various fields.
 
• He was a strong advocate of using statistical tools for economic planning and policy-making in India.
 
 
 
• **Recognition:**
 
 
• Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis was awarded the prestigious **Padma Vibhushan** in **1968** for his contributions to science and public service.
 
• His birth anniversary, **June 29**, is celebrated as **National Statistics Day** in India to honor his legacy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Second Five-Year Plan:**

 
 
• This plan, heavily influenced by Mahalanobis, aimed to establish a socialistic pattern of society by focusing on the growth of industries and reducing inequalities.
 
• It marked a shift from agriculture to industrialization as the main driver of economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Planning Commission of India:**
 
 
• The Planning Commission was established in **1950** to assess and allocate resources for the country's development plans.
 
• Mahalanobis served as a key advisor, shaping India's economic strategy during the early years of independence.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Mahalanobis is remembered as a pioneer in applying statistical methods to solve real-world problems in India.
 
• His work laid the foundation for the country's economic planning and scientific research in statistics.

questions.question: There are broadly_________ sets of factors that influence migration.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Migration** is influenced by broadly **two sets of factors**: **push factors** and **pull factors**.
 
• **Push factors** refer to conditions that compel individuals to leave their place of origin, such as **poverty, unemployment, lack of resources, natural disasters, and political instability**.
 
• **Pull factors** refer to conditions that attract individuals to a new location, such as **better job opportunities, higher standard of living, access to education, and social stability**.
 
• These two sets of factors operate in tandem and are central to understanding the dynamics of migration globally and locally.
 
• **Social, economic, and environmental reasons** are often categorized under push and pull factors, making these two sets the primary frameworks for analyzing migration. ***Hence, the correct answer is 1.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Push Factors:**

 
 
• **Poverty:** Lack of financial resources and economic opportunities often forces individuals to migrate to regions with better prospects.
 
• **Unemployment:** High unemployment rates in the region of origin push individuals to seek work elsewhere.
 
• **Natural Disasters:** Events like floods, earthquakes, and droughts displace people and lead to migration.
 
• **Political Instability:** Conflict, war, and oppressive regimes are significant reasons for forced migration.
 
 
 
• **Pull Factors:**
 
 
• **Employment Opportunities:** Availability of jobs and higher wages attract individuals to specific regions.
 
• **Better Living Standards:** Access to healthcare, education, and improved infrastructure acts as a pull factor.
 
• **Safety and Stability:** Political and social stability in the destination regions encourage migration.
 
• **Urbanization:** Cities often provide better economic and social opportunities, attracting migrants.
 
 
 
• **Types of Migration:**
 
 
• **Internal Migration:** Movement within the same country, often from rural to urban areas.
 
• **International Migration:** Movement across national borders, often for economic opportunities or safety.
 
• **Seasonal Migration:** Temporary movement due to seasonal work, such as agricultural labor.
 
 
 
• **Global Statistics:** According to the **International Organization for Migration (IOM)**, there were an estimated **281 million international migrants** globally in **2020**, highlighting the significance of migration factors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic Migration:** Driven primarily by financial factors such as better job opportunities or wages.
 
• **Forced Migration:** Includes refugees and internally displaced persons due to wars, natural disasters, or persecution.
 
• **Urban-Rural Divide:** Migration often occurs due to disparities in opportunities between urban and rural areas.
 
• **Policy Frameworks:** Countries often implement migration policies influenced by factors like workforce needs and humanitarian considerations.
 
• **Historical Context:** Migration has been a constant in human history, driven by the search for resources, safety, and better living conditions.

questions.question: Rig Veda is a collection of approximately how many hymns?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1028**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rig Veda** is one of the oldest sacred texts in the world and holds a prominent place in the **ancient Indian Vedic literature**.
 
• It is a collection of **1028 hymns** (suktas) written in **Vedic Sanskrit**, divided into **10 books or Mandalas**.
 
• These hymns are primarily dedicated to various **deities** such as Agni (fire), Indra (rain and thunderstorms), Varuna (cosmic order), and Soma (a sacred ritual drink).
 
• The Rig Veda is part of the **four Vedas**, which include the Yajur Veda, Sama Veda, and Atharva Veda. It is considered the oldest and most important among them.
 
• The hymns in the Rig Veda were composed between **1500 BCE and 1200 BCE**, during the early Vedic period in ancient India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of the Rig Veda:**

 
 
• The Rig Veda is divided into **10 Mandalas** (books), which vary in size and thematic content.
 
• The **10th Mandala** contains the famous **Purusha Sukta**, which describes the creation of the universe and the caste system.
 
• Each hymn (sukta) is composed of multiple **verses** (Riks), written in a poetic meter.
 
 
 
• **Language and Composition:**
 
 
• The hymns are written in **Vedic Sanskrit**, which is an ancient form of the Sanskrit language.
 
• The composition was oral, passed down through generations using precise **recitation techniques**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Rig Veda:**
 
 
• The Rig Veda provides deep insights into the **religious, philosophical, and social life** of early Vedic civilization.
 
• It is a key source for understanding the **mythology** and rituals of ancient India.
 
 
 
• **Other Vedas:**
 
 
• **Yajur Veda:** Contains instructions for performing rituals and sacrifices.
 
• **Sama Veda:** Focuses on melodies and chants used in rituals.
 
• **Atharva Veda:** Includes hymns, spells, and incantations for daily life and healing.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The Rig Veda reflects a pastoral and agrarian society where natural forces were deified and worshipped.
 
• It showcases the transition from a nomadic lifestyle to settled agriculture in the **Indo-Gangetic plain**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Compilation:** The Rig Veda was likely compiled by ancient sages known as the **Rishis**, including Vishwamitra, Vashishta, and others.
 
• **Preservation:** The oral tradition of **shruti** (hearing) and **smriti** (memory) ensured the accurate transmission of the text over centuries.
 
• **Global Recognition:** The Rig Veda is recognized as a UNESCO **Memory of the World** document for its historical significance.
 
• **Philosophical Ideas:** Concepts such as **Rta** (cosmic order) and **Yajna** (sacrifice) play a central role in the hymns.
